description: This circular chart visually organizes core principles of medical ethics into three main categories—Beneficence, Justice, and Autonomy—each represented by a distinct colored segment radiating from a central blue circle labeled “Beneficence.” The “Beneficence” segment, occupying the largest portion of the chart in a bright blue color, is subdivided into numerous smaller slices, including “Provide Medical Care to Patients,” “Continual Learning,” “Respect and Cooperate with Colleagues,” “Respect Life, Dignity of Patients,” “Give Top Priority to Patient’s Interest,” “Minimizing Conflicts of Interest,” “Ethical research,” “Open Discussion and Fair Charging of Fees,” “Comply with Laws and Regulations,” and “Recognize the Responsibility of the Occupation.” The “Justice” segment, shown in orange, contains slices such as “Promote Environmental Sustainability,” “Promote the Health of Community and Public Education,” “Allocate Medical Sources Fairly,” and “Treat Patients Fairly and Equally.” The “Autonomy” segment, colored green, includes slices like “Physician Can Freely Choose Whom to Serve,” “Make Responsible and Independent Clinical Judgement,” “Keep Confidential,” “Maintain Truthful, Factual Communication,” “Respect Patient’s Rights to be Informed, Freedom of Choice,” “Respect the Decision-making of Incompetent/Competent Patient,” and “Maintain Confidentiality.” Each slice contains its respective text label, and while no explicit percentage values or numerical data are shown, the relative sizes of the slices visually indicate their proportional contribution to each main category. The chart does not include a legend, nor do any slices have percentage labels or visual emphasis such as being exploded or bolded. The segments appear arranged in a clockwise order, generally descending in size from left to right within each main category.
